findings.finding: The NIQ RSM (CGA) Hospitality Business Tracker, the series MAB cites as its 'market', fell to flat LFL in October 2026 (pubs +0.4%, the weakest since April; restaurants +0.8%; bars -3.1%) from +2.7% in September. MAB's first ~8 weeks of FY27 therefore probably show a clear slowdown against last year's +3.8% first-8-weeks figure, which drove a +12.7% results day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Current-trading LFL at FY results: +3.8% first 8 weeks with FY25 results, stock +12.7% (28 Nov 2025). Q3 flat LFL, -5.1% (23 Jul 2026). H1 results with flat profit, -6.9% (21 May 2026). This line moves the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an industry proxy, not a MAB number. The stock is still about 10% above its pre-close price (306p vs 278p on 24 Sep), so the market has not priced a weak first eight weeks. If it had, the 60-day run-up would have unwound towards the pre-close level, not just the last 5 days' -3.6%.
findings.independence: September tracker +2.7% (https://www.restaurantonline.co.uk/Article/2026/10/22/september-proves-to-be-a-boom-month-for-hospitality-groups/) sets the base; Vinetur's write-up of the same release (https://www.vinetur.com/en/amp/20261118111375/britains-hospitality-groups-posted-flat-october-sales-after-five-months-of-growth.html) is the same data, not independent

findings.finding: Listed peers that reported after MAB's 24 Sep pre-close traded strongly into the festive period: Fuller's raised FY27 profit guidance, with LFL +5.8% over 32 weeks to 7 Nov and Christmas bookings +16% (c.11 Nov); Young's posted 6-week post-period LFL +5.1% (12 Nov); Wetherspoon reported LFL +8.2% over 14 weeks, 7.5% in the latest 5 (4 Nov).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MAB's festive/Q1 commentary has moved it +6.6% (Jan 2025 Q1) and +1.5% (Jan 2026 Q1); the FY results' outlook paragraph has mattered more than the reported year.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: MAB rose to about 319p by 6 Nov as these prints came out, then gave back about 4%. These peers are wet-led or London-heavy, while MAB is food-led and mass-market (Toby, Harvester), which is why the tracker and the peers diverge. MAB has not said where it sits between them.
findings.independence: Young's interims https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/youngs-posts-record-half-year-profit-after-strong-summer-trading ; Wetherspoon Q1 RNS https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/wetherspoon-j-d---jdw/trading-update-announcement/9856806 ; RSM's own note of 'healthy festive bookings' in the October tracker release

findings.finding: The 28 Oct 2026 Budget confirmed the National Living Wage rising 3.9% to £13.21 from April 2027, against 4.1% the year before. A 20% business-rates cut for pubs from April 2027 had been confirmed in July. Both fit, or slightly ease, MAB's guided FY27 cost headwind of c.£95m (c.4% of the cost base).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cost-headwind guidance: the FY25 results flagged rising costs and the stock still rose 12.7% on trading; at H1, profit held flat under cost pressure and the stock fell 6.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it lands inside a guide the company has repeated three times, the last after the July rates announcement. The only unpriced part is whether the £95m comes down a few £m, and the company has not said.

findings.finding: H1 FY26 cash flow included a £45m working-capital inflow 'due to payment timing differences'. If it reverses by year end, FY net cash flow and net-debt reduction will look weaker than the H1 run-rate implied.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to MAB cash flow alone; the FY25 results led with a £146m net-debt reduction and rose 12.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts model timing reversals, so most of this is in the estimates. What remains unpriced is the size of the reversal, which matters given the higher capex (£117m in H1) and £11m of Pesto contingent consideration.

findings.finding: Odyzean Limited controls 57.03% of MAB after a June 2026 market purchase, so the free float is about 43% with no disclosed short at or above 0.5%. That concentrates the reaction in a smaller float, but no change has been disclosed since June.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separable from the results reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and has no direction for this print. It bears on the size of the move, which is why it sits at 0 here and in abs_move_pct.

outside_window.finding: Pubs business-rates cut of 20% and the NLW rise both take effect April 2027, so their profit effect lands in FY27 H2, after the window; only the guide that reflects them is inside
